question.prompt: In the complex plane, let \(A\) be the set of solutions to \(z^3 - 8 = 0\) and let \(B\) be the set of solutions to \(z^3 - 8z^2 - 8z + 64 = 0.\) What is the greatest distance between a point of \(A\) and a point of \(B?\)

solutions.title: Factor and compare distances
solutions.explanation:
Factoring gives only a few points to compare, and conjugate points have equal distances to every point on the real axis.

For the first polynomial, the difference-of-cubes identity gives
\[
z^3-8=(z-2)(z^2+2z+4).
\]
The quadratic equation becomes \((z+1)^2=-3\), so its solutions are \(-1\pm i\sqrt3\), where \(i^2=-1\). Thus
\[
A=\{2,-1+i\sqrt3,-1-i\sqrt3\}.
\]

For the second polynomial, grouping terms gives
\[
z^3-8z^2-8z+64
=z^2(z-8)-8(z-8)
=(z-8)(z^2-8).
\]
Therefore,
\[
B=\{-2\sqrt2,2\sqrt2,8\},
\]
and all three points lie on the real axis.

A complex number \(x+iy\) represents the point \((x,y)\), whose squared distance to a real number \(t\) is \((x-t)^2+y^2\). Applying this formula gives the following table. The two conjugate roots share a row because changing the sign of \(y\) leaves \(y^2\) unchanged.

| Point in \(A\) | \(t=-2\sqrt2\) | \(t=2\sqrt2\) | \(t=8\) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| \(2\) | \(12+8\sqrt2\) | \(12-8\sqrt2\) | \(36\) |
| \(-1\pm i\sqrt3\) | \(12-4\sqrt2\) | \(12+4\sqrt2\) | \(84\) |

This accounts for every pair of points. Every entry in the first two columns is at most \(12+8\sqrt2<28\), while the last column contains \(36\) and \(84\). Hence the greatest squared distance is \(84\).

The greatest distance is \(\sqrt{84}=\boxed{2\sqrt{21}}\), choice \(\textbf{D}\).

solutions.title: Use the circle of cube roots
solutions.explanation:
The cube roots of \(8\) lie on a circle of radius \(2\), which helps us rule out the two smaller real roots of the second polynomial.

Write a nonzero complex number as
\[
z=r(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta),
\]
where \(r\) is its distance from the origin and \(\theta\) is its direction angle. Cubing cubes the distance and triples the angle:
\[
z^3=r^3(\cos3\theta+i\sin3\theta).
\]
Thus \(z^3=8\) requires \(r=2\), with the three distinct directions
\[
\theta=0^\circ,120^\circ,240^\circ.
\]
These locate all three points of \(A\).

Factoring the other polynomial gives
\[
z^3-8z^2-8z+64
=z^2(z-8)-8(z-8)
=(z-8)(z^2-8),
\]
so \(B=\{8,2\sqrt2,-2\sqrt2\}\).

For either point \(\pm2\sqrt2\), a path from a point of \(A\) through the origin has length \(2+2\sqrt2\). The straight-line distance cannot exceed this path length, so every such distance is less than \(6\). But \(2\in A\) is already distance \(6\) from \(8\). Therefore, a greatest-distance pair must use \(8\in B\).

The point of \(A\) in direction \(0^\circ\) is \(2\), giving distance \(6\). Each other point makes a \(120^\circ\) angle at the origin with the positive real axis. By the law of cosines, its squared distance to \(8\) is
\[
2^2+8^2-2(2)(8)\cos120^\circ
=68-32\left(-\frac12\right)
=84.
\]
Since \(84>6^2\), the greatest distance is \(\boxed{2\sqrt{21}}\), choice \(\textbf{D}\).
